title: Launch from a moving source: frame conversion before projectile motion

authority_basis.claim_scope: Object velocity in the ground frame equals object velocity relative to the moving source plus source velocity in the ground frame under Galilean kinematics.

concepts.statement: Each velocity is named by moving object and observation frame before vectors are combined.
concepts.why_required: Velocity addition is only meaningful when each velocity's object and reference frame are explicit.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Relative and ground-frame velocities can be combined in the wrong direction or interpreted as the same quantity.

concepts.statement: At release the object retains the source translational velocity contribution in the ground frame; release does not erase it.
concepts.why_required: The projectile initial condition in the ground frame must include source motion at the instant of release.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: The projectile is incorrectly treated as if launched from a stationary source.

model_conditions.condition: Relative velocities are combined under classical Galilean kinematics.
model_conditions.physical_reason: At ordinary speeds the release velocity transforms by vector addition between inertial frames.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: At relativistic speeds the velocity transformation law changes.

model_conditions.condition: The release event does not contain an impulsive horizontal interaction that cancels the source velocity contribution.
model_conditions.physical_reason: Velocity is continuous through ordinary release under the stated model.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: An impulse must be modelled explicitly in the release state.

representations.semantic_geometry: Three labelled velocity vectors form the Galilean relation between object-relative, source-ground and object-ground velocities at the release event.
must_not_imply: frame conversion can be performed after projectile evolution without changing initial conditions
representations.verification_method: Reverse the frame conversion and check the zero-source-speed limit recovers the ordinary stationary-launch case.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Name the object and observation frame for every velocity before calculation.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Different relative velocities can be conflated as the same physical quantity.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Convert the release velocity into the chosen ground frame by Galilean vector addition.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Projectile evolution begins from a velocity expressed in the wrong frame.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Only after frame conversion, resolve the ground-frame launch velocity and apply the ordinary projectile model with one post-release clock.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Relative-source components may be inserted directly into ground-frame projectile equations.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Verify by inverse frame conversion and the zero-source-speed limiting case.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: A sign or frame error can survive the forward solution.

required_transformations.description: Translate verbal motion into explicit object/frame velocity labels before any vector addition.
Convert velocities at release into the ground frame, then feed only the resulting ground-frame state into the projectile model.
Invert the Galilean relation to verify frame consistency and expose sign errors.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: Once the ball leaves the moving source it loses the source's horizontal velocity contribution.
misconceptions.why_plausible: The physical contact ends at release, which can be confused with the disappearance of the object's instantaneous velocity state.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: An object simply dropped from a uniformly moving cart still travels horizontally relative to the ground after release.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Show the source-ground vector as part of the object's ground-frame resultant at the release event.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Velocity is continuous through release under the model; gravity changes the vertical component but does not cancel inherited horizontal motion.
misconceptions.verification: Set source speed to zero to recover the stationary-source case, then invert the velocity-addition relation.

problem_families.name: Projectile launched from a moving source
recognition_cues: release or throw relative to moving source
problem_families.first_technical_move: Name all velocity frames and perform the release-frame conversion before projectile equations.
fatal_errors: using source-relative velocity directly in ground-frame projectile equations

problem_families.name: Infer a relative launch from ground-frame data
problem_families.first_technical_move: Write the velocity relation with explicit object/frame labels and invert it algebraically as a vector equation.
fatal_errors: subtracting unsigned speeds instead of vectors

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Move projectile evolution before frame conversion in the reasoning graph.
